market_context: United States and general English-speaking market
title: Peanut butter vs. almond butter

seo.title: Peanut butter vs. almond butter: nutrition comparison
seo.meta_description: Per 32 g, peanut butter has ~188 calories and 7.7 g protein; almond butter ~206 calories, 6.7 g protein and 3.1 g fiber. Compare minerals and vitamin E.
seo.search_intent: Compare peanut butter and almond butter for protein, fiber, calories and micronutrients

excerpt: In an equal 32 g serving, the USDA peanut-butter reference provides about 188 calories, 7.7 g protein, 15.8 g fat and 2.0 g fiber. Almond butter provides about 206 calories, 6.7 g protein, 17.0 g fat and 3.1 g fiber. Peanut butter leads slightly in protein; almond butter provides more fiber, calcium, magnesium and vitamin E.
content_html:
Peanut and almond butter are much closer nutritionally than price or health-halo marketing can imply. Peanut butter provides a little more protein; almond butter is higher in fiber, calcium, magnesium and vitamin E in the USDA references compared here.

Compare an equal 32 g serving

Per 32 gPeanut butterAlmond butter
Calories~188~206
Protein~7.7 g~6.7 g
Fat~15.8 g~17.0 g
Fiber~2.0 g~3.1 g
Calcium~16 mg~84 mg
Magnesium~62 mg~86 mg
Vitamin E~1.7 mg~5.4 mg

These are plain USDA Foundation reference foods. Sweeteners, salt and added oils can change a branded spread substantially.

The protein gap is small

Peanut butter provides about 24 g protein/100 g and almond butter 20.8 g. At 32 g, that is only about 1 g difference. They remain in the same general protein range.

Almond butter brings more fiber and minerals

The almond reference contains 9.7 g fiber/100 g versus 6.3 g in peanut butter. It also provides about 264 mg calcium and 268 mg magnesium/100 g, compared with about 50 and 193 mg.

The calcium difference is particularly visible: roughly 84 mg versus 16 mg in a 32 g serving.

Vitamin E is another clear almond advantage

Almond butter contains about 17 mg alpha-tocopherol/100 g compared with 5.4 mg in peanut butter. A 32 g serving works out to about 5.4 versus 1.7 mg.

Ingredients can matter more than prestige

A 100% peanut spread may be a simpler choice than an almond butter with sugar and added oil—or the reverse. The nut or legume base does not cancel out a very different formulation.

If both products are essentially 100% nuts/seeds, choose by taste, price and the nutrient you care about. Neither needs to be treated as the universally healthier version of the other.

faq.question: Which has more protein?
faq.answer: Peanut butter in these references: about 24 versus 20.8 g/100 g, roughly 1 g more per 32 g.

faq.question: Which has more fiber?
faq.answer: Almond butter: about 9.7 versus 6.3 g/100 g.

faq.question: Which has more calcium?
faq.answer: Almond butter by a wide margin in these references: about 264 versus 50 mg/100 g.

faq.question: Is almond butter always healthier?
faq.answer: No. Added sugar, oil and salt can matter as much as the base ingredient.
